title: ERP GPT endpoint knowledge-base document
description: Every file in kb/ (except this one) must validate against this schema. One file per GraphQL endpoint, named exactly after the endpoint: topCustomers.json documents topCustomers. CI enforces that every endpoint in the GraphQL schema has a matching KB file. RULE: no business data anywhere in these files — endpoint documentation only.

endpoint.description: Exact GraphQL field name, camelCase. Must match the schema.

description.description: One or two plain-English sentences: what this endpoint answers. Write for a salesperson, not a developer.

params.description: Every parameter the endpoint accepts. Empty array if none.

type.description: GraphQL type, e.g. Int, Date, String, or an enum name

example_questions.description: THE HIGHEST-LEVERAGE FIELD IN THIS FILE. These are what get embedded — retrieval matches user questions against these, one vector each. Write them the way sales/finance people actually talk, not developer English. Include at least one Roman-Urdu phrasing where natural. Minimum 4, aim for 5-8.

graphql.description: A complete, valid example query using $variables for parameters. The model copies this shape.

returns.description: Plain-English description of what comes back, e.g. 'List of customer names with summed revenue'.

do_not_use_when.description: Disambiguation against sibling endpoints. If two endpoints could be confused (salesByRegion vs revenueByRegion), this field is how the model tells them apart. Name the endpoint to use instead.

notes.description: Anything else the model needs: date format expectations, limit ceilings, timezone behaviour.
